subject.title: Feature Request: Batch API support for background tasks

question: Should OpenClaw add a provider-neutral delayed agent-turn lifecycle, and which provider and background entry point should form the first supported scope?
rationale: Provider jobs that outlive a streaming turn affect public SDK, protocol, persistence, cancellation, accounting, fallback, and result-delivery contracts, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent semantics.

options.title: Shared delayed-turn contract
options.body: Design submit, poll, cancel, resume, accounting, and result delivery once, then launch with one provider and cron agentTurn as the first consumer.

options.title: Cron-only provider experiment
options.body: Implement a narrowly scoped cron/provider path first, accepting that later generalization may require migration or API redesign.

options.title: Defer batch execution
options.body: Retain immediate streaming turns until the lifecycle complexity receives explicit roadmap sponsorship.

recommendation.title: Shared delayed-turn contract
recommendation.body: Design submit, poll, cancel, resume, accounting, and result delivery once, then launch with one provider and cron agentTurn as the first consumer.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history and discussion evidence connects this person to the central provider-runtime and cron product boundaries.
